governing_document.reason: Document 2026-18423 is a correction to AD 2026-17-03 that republishes the entire regulatory text. It corrects a typographical error in paragraph (g). Its text controls wherever it differs from the final rule 2026-16954. The only difference is in paragraph (g).

corrections.original_text: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.
corrections.corrected_text: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.

eligible_parts.description: A 3rd stage HPC rotor blade having P/N 6C8368, 6C8403, or later approved P/N. The 'later approved P/N' clause is open-ended and cannot be screened as a fixed list.
A 3rd stage HPC rotor blade modified to P/N 6A8353-001 or P/N 6A8688-001.

required_actions.description: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date of this AD where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed, replace the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades with parts eligible for installation.
required_actions.condition_description: The 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed at that engine shop visit.

ambiguities.description: Paragraph (g) uses the phrase 'where the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is exposed'. It does not use the defined term '3rd stage HPC rotor blade exposure' from (h)(2), and no paragraph of the governing text uses that defined term. It is therefore unclear whether (h)(2) sets the condition for (g). This affects which shop visits trigger the replacement.
readings: The condition is met only when any 3rd stage HPC rotor blade is removed from the HPC stage 3 to 8 drum, applying the (h)(2) definition to 'is exposed'.

The condition is met whenever the 3rd stage HPC rotor blades are made accessible or visible during the shop visit (for example, by HPC case or module disassembly), even if no blade is removed from the drum, because 'is exposed' is not the defined term and takes its ordinary meaning.

notes: The proposed rule (2025-20088) made the action due 'At the next 3rd stage HPC rotor blade exposure after the effective date'. In response to a United Airlines comment, the final rule changed this to the next engine shop visit after the effective date at which the blade is exposed, and added (h)(3).

The preamble states the FAA does not intend to require compliance for engines inducted into a shop visit before the effective date. (h)(3) defines 'engine shop visit' as the induction of an engine into the shop for maintenance.
Paragraph (g) states no flight-cycle or calendar backstop limit. The action is due only at a qualifying shop visit.

Paragraph (g) requires replacing the full set of 3rd stage HPC rotor blades, not only the blades with P/N 6A8353 or 6A8688. applies_to is recorded as part_condition_parts because the action acts on the 3rd stage HPC rotor blade set named in the part condition.
affected_parts is empty because no required action lists specific parts. The P/Ns 6A8353 and 6A8688 appear only in the applicability paragraph (c) and are recorded as the part condition.

The preamble states that replacing the blades per IAE AG SB V2500-ENG-72-0716, dated October 4, 2024, demonstrates compliance. That service bulletin is not referenced in or incorporated into the regulatory text; paragraph (k) states no material is incorporated by reference.
The preamble notes operators may request an AMOC under (i)(1) to extend the compliance time if parts are unavailable.
Paragraph (f) states 'Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.'
The final rule's Background says P/Ns 6A8353 'and' 6A8688, whereas the regulatory text (c) says 'P/N 6A8353 or P/N 6A8688'. The regulatory text controls.
The correction 2026-18423 states the effective date remains September 24, 2026.
